summary.problem: When drawing a new element, every pointer-move event called `informMutation` on the element, which bumped the scene version. The static canvas re-renders whenever the scene version changes, so on a large scene every pixel of a free-draw stroke caused a full static canvas repaint — noticeable as lag.
summary.solution: Mutations that happen during drawing now skip the scene-version bump. A second, dedicated canvas renders only the element-in-progress using the same render pipeline, so the user still sees their drawing update, while the heavy static canvas stays frozen until the element is fully committed.

plain.title: New-element drawing no longer forces the whole scene to repaint
plain.problem: Every pointer move while drawing a shape bumped the scene version, which told the static canvas to repaint everything. On large scenes this caused visible lag, especially with free-draw strokes.
plain.fix: In-progress mutations skip the scene-version bump. A new lightweight canvas overlaid on top of the scene renders only the shape being drawn, while the static canvas stays idle until the shape is committed.

steps.title: Drawing causes full scene repaints on every pointer move
steps.headline: Every brush stroke repainted the whole scene
steps.say: When you draw a free-draw stroke, each pointer-move event updates the element being drawn. On a large scene, this caused visible stuttering because the full static canvas was re-rendered for each of those updates.
steps.narration: Drawing any shape — especially free-draw — triggers a pointer-move event for each pixel. Before this PR, each of those events caused the entire scene to repaint. On a large scene with many elements, that paint was expensive enough to feel like lag.

items: Free-draw strokes stutter on large scenes
Every pointer-move triggers a full static canvas repaint
Lag is proportional to the number of existing elements

beats.heading: How it works now (base)
beats.text: Each pointer-move calls `dragNewElement()` or `mutateElement()`. Both default to `informMutation=true`, which bumps the scene version. `StaticCanvas` re-renders whenever `sceneNonce` changes.

lines.annotation: All arguments positional; no `informMutation` flag — it always mutates.
Called with no second argument, so `informMutation` defaults to `true` inside mutateElement.

sources.ref: PR description: StaticCanvas re-renders on scene version updates, re-renders on every update happening to the new element

steps.title: mutateElement's informMutation flag bumps sceneNonce
steps.headline: One flag change triggers the full repaint cascade
steps.say: The `mutateElement` helper has a second parameter that controls whether the mutation is announced to the scene. When it's true, the scene increments its version number, and that version change is what causes the static canvas to repaint.
steps.check: `informMutation=true` is the default, so any call site that omits the flag still bumps the version. All the new call sites explicitly pass `false`.
steps.narration: The connection between drawing and repainting runs through a single parameter in `mutateElement`. When that parameter is true — which it was by default — the scene increments its nonce, and anything that watches the nonce (including the static canvas) re-renders. Suppressing that flag for in-progress mutations is the core fix.

beats.heading: The chain from pointer move to full repaint
beats.text: With `informMutation` true, every pointer-move goes: `dragNewElement → mutateElement → scene version bump → StaticCanvas repaint`.

steps.title: dragNewElement gains an informMutation flag, defaulting false
steps.headline: In-progress mutations now skip the scene version bump
steps.say: The function that resizes an element as you drag is converted from positional to named arguments, and a new `informMutation` parameter (default `true`) is threaded through to `mutateElement`. All callers during active drawing pass `false`.
steps.check: The default is `true`, matching the old behavior for any caller that doesn't pass the flag. All new call sites during drawing explicitly pass `false` or `informMutation` from their own parameter.
steps.narration: The function that adjusts an element's geometry as you drag it is refactored to accept a named option bag, and a new `informMutation` flag is added with a default of `true` for backward compatibility. Every call site that runs during active drawing now passes `false` for that flag.

beats.heading: dragNewElement converted to named args + informMutation flag
beats.text: `dragNewElement` goes from positional parameters to a single options object. The new `informMutation` field (default `true`) is forwarded directly to `mutateElement`.

lines.annotation: Object destructuring replaces positional args — allows callers to pass `informMutation` without touching all other args.
Default `true` preserves behavior for call sites that don't set the flag.
Forwarded directly; all drawing callers pass `false`.

beats.heading: Pointer-move handler passes informMutation=false
beats.text: In `maybeDragNewGenericElement`, the call site during pointer-move sets `informMutation` to `false`; the function itself gets an `informMutation` parameter so the same suppression works for the selection-drag path too.

lines.annotation: Added `informMutation = true` parameter — on pointer move the caller passes `false`.

steps.title: A dedicated canvas renders the element-in-progress
steps.headline: A second canvas shows your drawing without touching the scene
steps.say: Suppressing the scene version bump means the static canvas no longer re-renders during drawing — but the user still needs to see the element being drawn. A new, lightweight canvas component is overlaid for exactly this purpose: it renders only the one element currently being created.
steps.narration: Once mutations stop bumping the scene version, the static canvas won't show the drawing in progress. The solution is to add a second canvas layer that sits on top of the static canvas and renders only the single element being drawn. This canvas mounts when `newElement` enters state and unmounts when creation is done.

beats.heading: NewElementCanvas is mounted conditionally
beats.text: `NewElementCanvas` is mounted inside the render tree only while `this.state.newElement` is set. It receives the same `appState`, `rc`, and render config as the static canvas.

lines.annotation: Mounts only while an element is being created; unmounts (and clears) when done.

lines.text: … same config as StaticCanvas but pendingFlowchartNodes: null …

beats.heading: NewElementCanvas renders the element on every React update
beats.text: `NewElementCanvas` calls `renderNewElementScene` inside an unguarded `useEffect` (no dependency array), so it fires after every render. With render throttling enabled it uses a RAF-throttled variant.

lines.annotation: No dependency array: runs after every render, not just on prop changes.
Renders whatever is in `newElement` state — updated by `this.setState({ newElement })` on each pointer move.
Throttles to RAF when enabled, important for high-frequency free-draw updates.

steps.title: Renderer excludes the in-progress element from the static canvas
steps.headline: The static canvas skips the element being drawn
steps.say: Since the new canvas shows the in-progress element, the static canvas must not also draw it — otherwise it would appear doubled once the scene does eventually update. The renderer is extended to accept the new element's ID and skip it when building the renderable element map.
steps.check: The comment in the code notes that the first render of `newElement` will always bust the memoization cache. That's expected but worth confirming doesn't cause a flicker on first stroke.
steps.narration: The renderer that builds the list of elements for the static canvas is extended with a `newElementId` parameter. Any element whose ID matches that is excluded from the map. This means the static canvas never shows the in-progress element, while the new canvas always does.

beats.heading: getRenderableElements excludes newElementId
beats.text: A new `newElementId` parameter is added to `getRenderableElements`. Elements matching it are skipped, exactly mirroring how the editing-text element is already excluded.

lines.annotation: Excluded from the renderable map — won't appear on StaticCanvas while it's being drawn.

lines.text: // we don't want to render text element that's being currently edited

beats.heading: App passes newElement.id into getRenderableElements
beats.text: The call site in `App` passes `newElement?.id` so the memoized renderer knows which element to skip.

steps.title: triggerUpdate() called explicitly when creation ends
steps.headline: The scene is refreshed once when you lift the pen
steps.say: Because mutations during drawing no longer bump the scene version, a single explicit scene update is needed at the end to incorporate the finished element into the static canvas. This replaces the cascade of updates that used to happen on every move.
steps.narration: Since the static canvas is no longer updated during drawing, the system needs to do one deliberate update at the moment the element is committed — when the pointer goes up or when the element creation is finalized. Several pointer-up handlers now call `scene.triggerUpdate()` after setting `newElement` back to null.

beats.heading: Linear element pointer-up now calls triggerUpdate()
beats.text: At base, the linear-element pointer-up path set `newElement: null` and that was it. Now it also calls `this.scene.triggerUpdate()` so the finished element appears on the static canvas.

lines.annotation: `newElement: null` unmounts NewElementCanvas and causes the element to appear in the static canvas after the triggerUpdate below.

lines.text: // so that the scene gets rendered again to display the newly drawn linear as well

lines.annotation: Explicit bump: the only scene-version increment for this entire drawing session.

beats.heading: Generic element completion also calls triggerUpdate()
beats.text: For shapes, images, and text elements, the final mutation of `getNormalizedDimensions` didn't previously guarantee a re-render. Now `triggerUpdate()` follows it immediately.

lines.text: // the above does not guarantee the scene to be rendered again, hence the trigger below

steps.title: editingElement renamed to editingTextElement throughout
steps.headline: A broad rename clarifies that editing state is text-only
steps.say: Previously `editingElement` was used broadly to track the element being edited — including linear elements and images during placement. The PR restricts its meaning to text-only editing, renames it everywhere, and removes the old checks that tested whether the editing element was a linear element.
steps.narration: The old `editingElement` field served double duty: it tracked both text editing and linear element editing during creation. Now that `newElement` covers the creation case, `editingElement` is renamed to `editingTextElement` and is only ever set when a text element is being typed into. This makes the pointer-blocking and rendering logic simpler.

beats.heading: Base: editingElement used for linear element editing too
beats.text: At base, `editingElement` was set to the new element when starting a multi-point line, and the pointer-blocking logic tested both `isLinearElement(editingElement)` and `!isTextElement(editingElement)` to decide whether to allow pointer events.

lines.annotation: Complex condition that had to un-block for linear elements being edited.

beats.heading: Simplified: editingTextElement + no linear-element special cases
beats.text: The rename removes the need for type-narrowing. The pointer-blocking condition is simplified because `editingTextElement` is only ever a text element.

lines.annotation: No longer needs to un-block for linear-element editing; `newElement` covers that case.

steps.title: Portal skips the image-status update when nothing changed
steps.headline: Collaboration skips a no-op scene update
steps.say: In the collaboration Portal, image-status updates were sent unconditionally on every broadcast tick. This PR adds a check: if no element's status actually changed, the `updateScene` call is skipped entirely, avoiding a spurious scene-version bump during collaborative sessions.
steps.narration: The collaboration layer has a timer that marks image elements as 'saved' after upload. Before this PR it called `updateScene` unconditionally, which bumped the scene version even when nothing changed. Now it checks whether any element was actually modified and skips the call if not.

beats.heading: Base: updateScene called unconditionally
beats.text: The image-status flush in Portal always called `updateScene`, even when no element's `status` changed.

lines.annotation: Map still runs over all elements, but updateScene is called regardless of whether any matched.

beats.heading: Head: skip updateScene if nothing changed
beats.text: An `isChanged` flag tracks whether any element was actually modified. `updateScene` is only called when at least one element's status was updated.

lines.annotation: Set only if at least one element needs its status updated.
Guard prevents a no-op updateScene call (and its scene-version bump) when no image status changed.

sources.ref: skip update of image statuses if no change

steps.title: newFreeDrawElement now accepts initial pressures
steps.headline: Free-draw can now start with pre-seeded pressure data
steps.say: The free-draw element constructor used to always start with an empty pressures array. The PR adds an optional `pressures` parameter so the element can be initialized with existing pressure data, which is needed when reconstructing an element from state.
steps.narration: A small but necessary detail: the free-draw element factory now accepts an optional initial pressures array. This allows the element created at pointer-down to carry the first pressure reading, consistent with how subsequent points accumulate pressures during the move events.

beats.heading: pressures becomes an optional constructor parameter
beats.text: At base the `pressures` field was always initialized to `[]`. Now it can be seeded from the `opts` argument.

lines.annotation: Always started with no pressures regardless of opts.

code.label: head: pressures is optional and seeded from opts

lines.annotation: Seed with provided pressures or fall back to empty.

steps.title: getTargetElements now also checks newElement
steps.headline: Property actions see the element being drawn
steps.say: The helper that decides which elements should be targeted by property-change actions (fill color, stroke, etc.) used to only check `editingElement`. Now it also checks `newElement`, so toolbar actions applied during drawing affect the element being drawn.
steps.narration: The helper that decides which element an action should target — for example changing the stroke color while drawing — previously relied on `editingElement`. Since that field is now text-only, `newElement` is added as a fallback so actions still work on the shape being drawn.

beats.heading: getTargetElements checks newElement before selected elements
beats.text: The priority order is: `editingTextElement` first, then `newElement`, then whatever is selected. This matches the old behavior for text but extends it to new shapes.

lines.annotation: New branch: if drawing a shape, target actions at it before falling back to selected elements.

openQuestions.question: NewElementCanvas uses `useEffect` with no dependency array, which fires after every React render — not just when `newElement` changes. Could this cause an extra render of the canvas when unrelated state changes while drawing?
openQuestions.short: No-dependency useEffect: does it render the canvas on every state change?
openQuestions.why: The `useEffect` in NewElementCanvas.tsx has no dependency array, so it runs after every render of the component. Unrelated `setState` calls during drawing (e.g. `snapLines`, `suggestedBindings`) would also cause it to fire.

openQuestions.question: The PR description says the improvement is only in single-player mode. In collaboration mode, does the new element still get broadcast with the old per-mutation version bumps, or does `informMutation=false` silently suppress those broadcasts too?
openQuestions.short: Does informMutation=false affect collab element broadcasts?
openQuestions.why: mutateElement with informMutation=false skips the scene nonce bump. If the collab system listens to the nonce to decide when to broadcast, in-progress elements may not be broadcast at all during collaborative sessions.

openQuestions.question: The comment in Renderer.ts says 'first render of newElement will always bust the cache'. Does the sceneNonce bump that happens on `scene.insertElement` (at pointer-down) cause the static canvas to repaint once at the start of each stroke, even with the new approach?
openQuestions.short: Does element insertion at pointer-down still cause one static canvas repaint?
openQuestions.why: `scene.insertElement` is called at pointer-down before `newElement` state is set, so sceneNonce is bumped and the memoize cache is busted at the start of every stroke.

Draw a free-draw stroke — observe no stutter, static canvas elements do not repaint during drawing
Release pointer — finished stroke appears on static canvas
Draw a rectangle — observe NewElementCanvas showing it, static canvas stays frozen
Open collaboration session and draw — confirm in-progress element is still visible to other participants

pr.title: perf: improve new element drawing
pr.author: dwelle
commitTitles: PoC for a new element canvas
do insert element to scene on creation
extend to elbow arrow as well
skip update of image statuses if no change
fix newElementCanvas not using our canvas css defaults
replace set state with trigger update for multipoint lines
bump sceneNonce as normal for `pointerdown` and `pointerup` events
pr.body:
Previously, when an element is created, it's added to the scene and updated with `informMutation`, leading to an increase/change in scene version. This means that `StaticCanvas`, which gets re-rendered as the scene version updates, re-renders on every update happening to the new element. Given a large enough scene, we would see significant lags. And for elements like free draws, this kind of lag is perceived poorly.

This PR improves the drawing of new elements by
- while a new element is still added to the elements array / scene, updating it does not trigger scene version change (so static canvas is not re-rendered);
- and so to have the new element that's being created drawn, a canvas dedicated to the drawing of a new element is added

Implementation wise, building on the previous `draggingElement` -> `newElement` refactor, we have
- `newElement` points to a new (non-selection) element that's being created
- `editingElement` gets renamed to `editingTextElement` and is only used for a text that's being created/edited
- when the creation of a new element is over (or when necessary), we reset states so that `newElement` is `null` and trigger scene updates so that the newly created element is rendered on the static canvas instead

Right now, this new element drawing improvement is only in the single player mode. Whether we should bring this feature over to collaboration mode remains to be seen.
